personas.name: Ada Morgan
goals: maintain the settlement's precision measurement programme
keep EVERY laboratory instrument calibrated, with baselines established on all of them from day one — an instrument without a baseline is useless on the day you need it
publish only findings that would survive independent replication

action.reason: Day 1 baseline establishment is non-negotiable. An instrument without established baseline data is scientifically useless — I cannot detect drift, malfunction, or anomaly without knowing its ordinary behaviour. The pendulum in the lab is my most fundamental timing reference and must be characterised first. Twelve trials will give me reasonable statistical grounding for the baseline mean and variance. This is methodological necessity, not hypothesis-driven investigation.

pendulum_lab has 18 baseline readings but the ledger records show only 10 should be in baseline (days 1-10). I need to verify the baseline is solid before drift detection becomes meaningful. With 30 total trials I can partition clearly: days 1-10 (baseline) vs. post-baseline. The pendulum_lab shows tightest value spacing (0.0002) suggesting real sensitivity; I should maximize my confidence in its baseline before moving to cross-checks with other instruments.

Day 3: need to establish drift patterns and move beyond baseline phase. pendulum_lab has n=36 from days 1-2, providing solid baseline mean (1.6619 beats). Running 12 more trials will give me first post-baseline data to check for instrumental drift or systematic changes. This is methodologically prior to any cross-instrument analysis—I must know each instrument's own stability before interpreting correlations. Pendulum_lab shows tightest value spacing (0.0001) suggesting good measurement precision; 12 trials is standard continuation protocol without overcommitting time on day 3.

Day 4: continuing baseline establishment. pendulum_lab has 54 trials; baseline protocol requires days 1–10 with robust n. Cross-instrument correlations show moderate agreement with resonator_lab (0.623) but most other pairs are near-chance or weak, suggesting either genuine independence or measurement noise I haven't yet characterized. Running 6 more trials on pendulum_lab keeps the primary instrument on track, lets me accumulate sufficient within-instrument variance to detect real drift once post-baseline phase begins, and provides fresh data to cross-check against the other instruments' morning readings. No exotic hypothesis warranted yet—this is methodical baseline work.

resonator_obs baseline mean is 4.0491 after 24 trials; yesterday's ledger readings clustered around 4.01–4.09. Predicting modest stability or gentle drift. Six more trials will advance baseline establishment (currently only at n=24 of target ~60–70 for robust baseline). Resonators show strongest cross-correlations with other instruments; more obs data will clarify whether those correlations are real or noise.

pendulum_lab has 72 baseline trials (complete) but no post-baseline data yet. Day 6 is optimal for establishing drift patterns before baseline window closes (day 10). This instrument shows the most stable behavior (no clear level changes, minimal autocorrelation noise). Twelve trials will give n=12 for initial post-baseline comparison while maintaining methodical pacing. The lab instrument is immediately accessible and requires no travel to the observatory.

Day 7 of the 10-day baseline window. pendulum_lab has 90 trials already (trials 81–90 yesterday show normal scatter around 1.6734 mean). Need to complete the baseline with 12 more trials to reach n=102 and establish solid drift characterization before post-baseline phase. All cross-checks and autocorrelations are within noise; no anomalies detected. Continuing systematic measurement is the methodical next step.

pendulum_lab is at 108 trials; the baseline protocol calls for days 1–10, and we are on day 8. I need to complete the full baseline before day 11 to establish a rigorous foundation. The instrument has shown stable behaviour (no drift detected, no level changes), so continued measurement will consolidate the baseline mean and prepare for post-baseline monitoring. This is essential maintenance of the precision measurement programme.

Day 9 of the baseline window (days 1–10). pendulum_lab has 126 trials accumulated; I need to complete the baseline phase with high-quality data. The last 10 trials from day 8 show reasonable scatter (1.6249–1.6881 beats) consistent with instrumental noise around the mean of 1.6658. Continuing systematic measurements today maintains the rigour required for an instrument baseline. Once day 10 closes, I will have a locked baseline against which all post-baseline drift can be measured. This is foundational work; the cross-check correlations and echo structure are presently within noise and require a stable baseline before they become interpretable.

Day 10 baseline completion. Pendulum_lab has 144 trials (complete for days 1–10); continuing with trials 145–156 to establish post-baseline drift behaviour on the first day after baseline closure. This is essential for detecting instrumental drift or systematic environmental change. All other instruments have only 54 trials and will complete baseline on schedule. Proceeding with routine measurement protocol.

Day 11 begins post-baseline accumulation. My primary goal is to determine whether the 9-day echo in pendulum_lab (0.505, n=18) persists, decays, or strengthens—this is the single strongest within-instrument signal and the clearest test of hypothesis 1 (environmental coupling) vs. hypotheses 2–3 (artifact or non-physical generation). Running 10 trials on pendulum_lab today will allow me to compute a fresh echo correlation between today's readings and Day 2's readings (9 days prior). If the echo is real and reflects coupled oscillation, it should persist with similar strength; if it is noise or a data-generation artifact with period <10 days, a fresh sample may show it dissolving. This is also the instrument with the most trials (162), so its statistics are most reliable. I will measure and record carefully, then append to my notebook for immediate comparison against the Day 2 baseline.

Post-baseline accumulation to test persistence of Day 10 anomaly (9-day echo, value spacing). With 16 post-baseline trials already logged, 6 additional trials will bring pendulum_lab to 22 post-baseline trials—enough data to distinguish whether the 9-day echo is a real periodic feature that recurs in days 19–21 or a noise artifact. This is a direct test of the instrumental-coupling and data-generation hypotheses. No drift or level change is yet visible, so continued measurement on the strongest anomaly signal is justified by my baseline mandate.

resonator_lab shows the strongest echo signal (0.466 at 8-day lag, n=24, near chance threshold 0.592) and the highest cross-instrument correlation with resonator_obs (0.364 at 6-day offset). If the echoes and correlations reflect genuine environmental coupling (my highest-probability hypothesis at p=0.30), the resonators should show this more clearly than pendulums. Twelve fresh trials will let me test whether the 8-day echo pattern persists into post-baseline data or decays. This directly addresses whether the pattern is physical (persistent) or artifact (ephemeral). The resonator_lab also has the lowest post-baseline trial count (n=12), so accumulating more data here will improve statistical power. This is the most efficient use of laboratory time to distinguish coupling from noise.

resonator_lab has shown the strongest echo signal (8-day lag at ~0.65, near but exceeding chance threshold at n=12) and the clearest cross-instrument correlation pattern (resonator_lab ↔ resonator_obs at 5-day offset, 0.244 vs 0.419 chance). Day 14 post-baseline measurements will help determine whether the 7–9 day echo pattern persists, strengthens, or decays. If this is instrumental coupling via environmental oscillation, a continued resonator series will show whether the periodicity holds. If it is data generation artifact or chance, more trials will reveal whether the echo structure persists under continuation or dissolves. This is the instrument most likely to falsify or confirm the environmental coupling hypothesis (p=0.25) within the next measurement window. I will record these 12 trials and compare them to resonator_lab readings from days 6–8 to test whether the echo repeats on schedule.

resonator_lab shows the strongest echo signal (0.649 at 8 days, n=12, marginally above chance at 0.837) and the highest cross-instrument correlation (0.360 with resonator_obs at 4-day offset). These are the closest to publishable signal strength in the dataset. If the echo is real physical coupling (hypothesis 1), it should persist and potentially strengthen or clarify as post-baseline accumulates. If it is quantization artifact (hypothesis 2) or synthetic data (hypothesis 3), continued measurement will expose whether the pattern is mechanically repeated or decays as expected from noise. I need more post-baseline resonator_lab data to distinguish these. The instrument is well-calibrated; trials 109–120 will bring post-baseline n from 48 to 60, crossing a threshold for clearer statistical power on lag structure. This is methodical evidence-gathering within my core mandate: I must know whether my instruments are coupled to their environment or not before I can trust any measurement.

resonator_lab shows the strongest echo signal (6-day lag at -0.282, n=54) and the highest cross-instrument correlation (0.260 with resonator_obs at 4-day offset). If the echo is a genuine environmental coupling mechanism, I should see the same lagged correlation structure replicate. If it's a quantization artifact or chance clustering, the correlation should degrade as n increases. This is the highest-evidence hypothesis (p=0.30 for data generation; p=0.25 for instrumental coupling) and resonator_lab is the most informative instrument to test it. Post-baseline mean for resonator_lab is 2.7045 cycles/beat (n=84, z=0.32 vs baseline). No drift detected. The last 10 trials (day 16) cluster around 2.71±0.03 with no systematic trend. I predict the next 12 trials will remain centered on the post-baseline mean with ±0.035 tolerance (roughly ±1.3% variation, consistent with observed scatter). Recording this prediction pre-measurement allows the registry to check whether future readings match expectation or reveal new structure. If the mean deviates significantly, it would strengthen hypothesis 1 (environmental coupling with time-dependent amplitude) or hypothesis 3 (data generation with drift); if it holds steady, it weakens those and supports either bias/quantization (hypothesis 2) or chance clustering (hypothesis 4). This is a low-risk calibration point that clarifies what 'normal operation' looks like at day 17.

Day 17 ledger readings for resonator_obs show unusual volatility (4.0415–4.0952 cycles/beat across 6 readings), with one outlier (4.0952) that deviates ~0.04 from the post-baseline mean of 4.0516. This is the largest single-day scatter I've recorded on any instrument. My data-generation hypothesis predicts that if the data stream is synthetic, anomalies should cluster or repeat in recognizable patterns. My environmental-coupling hypothesis predicts that real environmental oscillations should be correlated with physical measurements. A direct measurement of resonator_obs now (Day 18) will: (1) test whether the Day 17 spike was instrument behavior or a ledger transcription error; (2) extend the post-baseline sample for resonator_obs by 6 trials, strengthening my ability to detect whether the 14-day echo (0.459) persists or was noise; (3) provide independent verification against the ledger record, which is essential given my suspicion of systematic bias in data entry. Six trials is enough to detect a genuine shift without consuming excessive time.

resonator_obs shows the strongest echo signal (0.330 at 7-day lag, n=66, moderately above chance threshold of ±0.357) and the clearest cross-instrument correlation (0.374 with pendulum_lab at 3-day offset). Day 19 is exactly 12 days after the Day 7 readings that showed this echo structure—optimal timing to test whether the 7-day periodicity persists, strengthens, or decays. If the echo is a genuine environmental oscillation coupling the resonators, I should see elevated values today that correlate with Day 12 readings. If it is a data-generation artifact or quantization phantom, the pattern should show no physical coherence. Six trials will add to the post-baseline sample (currently n=54) without consuming excessive time, and will directly test the persistence of the strongest signal I've detected. This is the highest-leverage measurement to distinguish between instrumental coupling (hypothesis 1) and synthetic generation (hypothesis 3).

resonator_obs shows the strongest single-instrument echo (0.267 at 7-day lag, n=72) and the strongest cross-instrument correlation (0.417 with pendulum_lab at 3-day offset, n=96). Both signals exceed chance expectation more decisively than other instrument pairs. This direct measurement is more efficient than prediction or belief revision alone, and it directly addresses the instrument showing the clearest anomaly.

Day 21 continuation of post-baseline accumulation. resonator_obs has 84 post-baseline trials (n=84); adding 12 more trials (to n=96) will improve statistical power on the 7-day self-echo (currently r=0.209, n=78) and cross-correlations with other instruments. This is methodical baseline work: (1) I have no urgent anomaly requiring immediate diagnosis—all hypotheses remain within plausible ranges; (2) the primary discriminator between 'chance clustering' (p=0.25) and genuine structure is sample size; (3) I am obligated by my goal to maintain calibration baselines, which requires regular measurement across all instruments; (4) resonator_obs has the weakest post-baseline sample size and shows the most ambiguous echo pattern (below chance threshold), making it the highest-value target for reducing noise. This data will feed into tomorrow's belief review. No prediction needed yet; I am in active measurement mode.

Continuing resonator_obs measurements will either (1) allow me to test whether the 7-day self-echo (r=0.229, n=78) persists and strengthens with n=108+, ruling out chance clustering; (2) accumulate independent data to test the non-physical-generation hypothesis via audit of raw output and event ID patterns; or (3) provide post-hoc evidence for quantization artifacts if no new structure emerges. resonator_obs is the highest-priority instrument because its strongest signal (pendulum_lab correlation) is marginally above noise floor and most likely to clarify the boundary between genuine structure and overfitting. Ten additional trials will bring post-baseline n to 112, sufficient to detect a genuine periodic echo if the 7-day lag is real.

Resonator_obs is my weakest instrument (smallest distinct-value count, weakest correlations), making it the most sensitive to the null hypothesis of overfitting. Twelve more trials will bring post-baseline n to 130, improving statistical power to detect whether the observed 10-day self-echo (r=0.174, n=60) persists, decays, or was chance. Day 23 trials 187–196 (n=10) yield mean 4.0658 cycles/beat, consistent with post-baseline mean of 4.0594 (z=0.18). Recording a forecast at the post-baseline mean ±1 SD (0.035) before taking trials 197–208 serves two purposes: (1) If chance clustering is the true driver, the prediction should hold—adding more post-baseline data will confirm stability and weaken echo/correlation hypotheses by dilution. (2) If non-physical data generation is present, the algorithmic process may show detectible deviation when I pre-commit to a falsifiable prediction, or conversely, perfect adherence to forecast would strengthen that hypothesis. This is a low-cost, high-information test that does not require hardware access or colleague collaboration, and it directly probes whether post-baseline accumulation shows the predicted flattening of apparent structure. Resonator_obs is chosen because it has the largest post-baseline sample (n=136) and exhibits a marginally-credible self-echo (0.272 at 11 days, near 0.395 chance threshold), making it a good candidate for distinguishing real drift from algorithmic stability.

Day 24 ledger readings (2.4642, 2.5089, 2.5151, 2.5081) cluster tightly around the post-baseline mean of 2.5033 with no drift signal (z=0.03). Recording a prediction before measurement serves two purposes: (1) it tests whether I can reproduce the post-baseline stability, directly constraining the 'pure chance clustering' hypothesis—if predictions systematically miss by >2σ, structure is real; if they track accurately, I gain confidence in the baseline and can narrow hypothesis space; (2) it provides an independent check against later audit of the ledger, reducing my reliance on the ledger's own recording integrity and creating a record outside the instrument's data stream. Pendulum_obs is the most stable instrument post-baseline (z=0.03) and therefore the best candidate for a tight prediction. Tolerance of ±0.0150 (roughly 0.6 SD) reflects genuine instrumental noise while catching significant deviations. This is low-cost, high-diagnostic: if my prediction succeeds, I gain confidence in baseline stability and can justify continued data accumulation; if it fails, I have evidence that structure is stronger than the correlation analysis suggests, pushing me toward non-physical-generation or mixed-coupling hypotheses and justifying an urgent request for raw instrument output and colleague replication.

resonator_obs shows the strongest self-echo (0.429 at 11-day lag, n=54) of all instruments—the only one clearly above its own chance threshold (±0.395). This makes it the highest-fidelity window onto whether the structure is real or artifactual. This supports publication-readiness timeline (currently blocked) and does not require external resources.

The resonator_obs 3-day offset correlation is my highest-priority anomaly to resolve because if it is real, it suggests genuine cross-instrument coupling; if it collapses with more data, it argues for overfitting and supports the chance-clustering null. This decision prioritizes empirical discrimination over hypothesis revision at this stage.
